# Retrospective: #12754 follow-up

## What worked

- Checking patch-id first confirmed that the linked `0dc9f9c` and the packet's `9fcf219` are the same PR content across a rebase. This avoided a false "changed code" reading.
- Cross-examination was cheap and useful. One Sol resume confirmed all four points that only Opus had raised.
- The Opus old-vs-head sealed run gave discriminating evidence for both fixes and for the new migration regression.

## Process deviations (minor, disclosed)

- **Opus:** ran one `git status --porcelain` in the pinned clone (read-only under `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, unnecessary).
- **Opus:** created `--shared` clones with checkouts under `opus/checkouts`, which are its own writes. It also listed and extracted the Vivaldi package archive host-side, into its output directory, after inspecting the members.
- **Sol:** extracted package UI files host-side, into its own directory, after inspecting the members.
- Neither reviewer executed package content.
- **Opus fixture guards:** accumulated mismatch rather than gating immediately, and per-command setup writes were not individually gated (see the REPORT evidence audit). Public claims were narrowed accordingly.
- **Coordinator:** the initial triage read the full PR diff via grep patterns rather than line-by-line, which suffices for injection triage but is not a full read. Reviewers read the relevant source.

## Improvements

- The brief could state explicitly whether host-side archive listing and extraction into the reviewer's own directory is permitted, so reviewers do not have to self-classify it.
- Omarchy follow-ups often hinge on caller `set -e` behavior. Naming "callers of changed status-returning commands" in neutral questions worked well.

## Omadev / tooling

None used.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12754#issuecomment-5791678764) and the [author reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12754#issuecomment-5795703846), checked at `1b66380`.

| Earlier finding | Outcome at `1b66380` |
|---|---|
| Force-dark preferences reset | **Resolved** |
| Vivaldi refresh failures reported as success | **Resolved** |
| Live theme channel shared across users | **Corrected:** cross-user color sharing withdrawn; narrower Vivaldi-specific ownership issue remains |

One new issue: now that the refresh status is reported, a refresh failure can stop `omarchy update` and other browser installs.

**Verified:** `omarchy-theme-set-vivaldi` no longer assigns either force-dark preference, and the updated `vivaldi-theme-test.sh` passes at `1b66380` and fails against the earlier writer. In an isolated run of the real refresh chain, preferences set to `true` stay `true`. In the Vivaldi 8.2.4133.64 UI, `vivaldi.appearance.force_dark_mode_theme` is the "Force a dark theme on all websites" setting, so it is unrelated to the UI theme. `omarchy-theme-set-browser` now records `|| failed=1` without clearing an earlier policy failure. The new aggregate test block passes at `1b66380` and fails against the earlier setter.

### Correction: multi-user channel

The author's point holds. `omarchy-theme-set-browser-policy` already writes `BrowserThemeColor` to machine-wide managed policy under `/etc`, so Chromium-family browsers already share the Omarchy color across accounts. The earlier review was wrong to present cross-user color sharing as a Vivaldi defect, and to suggest a Vivaldi-only per-user channel. That part is withdrawn, and deferring the broader multi-user design is consistent with the existing browser model.

These parts are specific to Vivaldi and remain (source-derived, only on installs where more than one account runs Omarchy):

- **Write access follows the last hook run.** Migration `1789981149` checks only whether the Vivaldi package is installed, so any account that runs its migrations or `omarchy update` becomes the owner of `style/omarchy.json`, even an account that never uses Vivaldi. Its installed post-update hook then takes ownership again on every update. Refreshes from other accounts skip the channel write without a status or message. Each account's loader still applies the owner's channel (colors and Hyprland appearance) into that account's profile at startup.
- **The running-browser check is not user-scoped.** `pgrep -x vivaldi` in `omarchy-theme-set-vivaldi` skips a profile update whenever any account's Vivaldi is running.

**Impact:** On installs where more than one account runs Omarchy, only the channel owner's theme changes reach the live channel. Every account's Vivaldi shows the owner's colors and Hyprland appearance, and one account's running Vivaldi blocks native profile updates for the others. None of this is reported.

**Suggested change:** Scoping the check to the current user (`pgrep -u "$UID" -x ...`) does not depend on any future multi-user model. A message when the channel is not writable would make the lock-out visible.

### Vivaldi refresh failures now stop `omarchy update` and other browser installs

Because `omarchy-theme-set-browser` now returns the refresh status, callers that stop on errors now stop on a refresh failure:

```text
omarchy update -> omarchy-migrate (bash -euo pipefail)
  -> migrations/1789981149.sh -> vivaldi-post-update (set -eu)
    -> omarchy-theme-set-browser -> vivaldi-theme-refresh exits 1
=> migration fails, no marker written, later migrations and update steps do not run
```

Two triggers persist across runs:

- **A theme without `accent`.** `docs/theming.md` describes `accent` as optional. `vivaldi-theme-refresh` runs `accent=$(omarchy-theme-color accent)` under `set -eu`, and `omarchy-theme-color` exits 1 for a missing key with no fallback. So the refresh exits before its own `|| exit 0` guard. `omarchy-theme-set-vivaldi` treats the same condition as a no-op.
- **A malformed, unreadable or unwritable Vivaldi `Preferences` file**, which makes the native writer exit 1.

In an isolated run using the real `omarchy-migrate`, migration and refresh chain (only the sudo part of `vivaldi-post-update` was modelled), both triggers stopped the migration queue at `1b66380`. At `9fcf219` the migration completed. Nothing was printed to stderr. From source, `omarchy-install-browser` (`set -e`) likewise exits after installing Chromium, Chrome, Edge or Brave when Vivaldi is installed and its refresh fails.

**Impact:** On a system with Vivaldi installed, either trigger makes every `omarchy update` fail at this migration until the theme or profile is fixed, with no hint pointing at Vivaldi. `migrations/1787515927.sh` already runs `omarchy-theme-set-browser || true` for this reason, with a comment calling the repaint cosmetic.

**Suggested change:** Keep the new aggregate status, and change the callers and the missing-color path:
- Make the refresh's color reads tolerate a missing key, as the native writer does (for example `omarchy-theme-color accent color4`, matching the documented fallback).
- Keep the one-shot migration from failing on the repaint, as `1787515927.sh` does.
- Print a short message when the Vivaldi refresh fails.

**Optional test improvement:** The new aggregate-status block in `browser-policy-dir-test.sh` checks only the `(0,1)`, `(1,0)` and `(1,1)` cases. In a synthetic run it still passed when `omarchy-theme-set-browser` was replaced by a script that always exits 1. Adding `run_browser_theme_set 0 0 || fail ...` catches that.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Follow-up limited to the three earlier findings, the author reply and the new commit's effect on callers. Source review of the changed files, callers and migration/update runners at `1b66380`. One isolated command-only run covered the refresh chain, `omarchy-migrate`, and the PR's two new test assertions at `1b66380` and `9fcf219`, with package-presence, `pgrep` and `hyprctl` stubbed. Vivaldi UI resources from the Arch 8.2.4133.64-2 package were read, not executed. Not run: Vivaldi or any GUI, the real `vivaldi-post-update` against `/opt`, `omarchy-install-browser`, the full `browser-policy-dir-test.sh`, and any multi-account setup. Multi-user behavior is source-derived.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments of this revision with targeted cross-checks of single-source points, and an Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
